units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 357:35">Sifré Deut. 357</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 34:7">Deut. XXXIV, 7</cite>) <he>א״ת לא נס לֵחֹה כל … ל׳ פורחת וכ׳</he>, <he>אלא נס לֵחֹה עכשיו</he> read not, ‘his moisture (vigor) had not failed’ but ‘was not failing now’ (that he was dead) (i.e. <cite ref="N00913"><he>נס</he></cite> is not meant for the perfect tense but for the partic. present), whoever touched Moses’ body, felt moisture burst forth from it in all directions; Yalk. ib. 963.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 2:1">Shebi. II, 1</cite> <he>עד שתכלה הל׳</he> until the moisture in the ground is gone; Y. ib. 33ᶜ <he>מאן תנא ל׳</he> what Tannai is it that makes moisture a condition?—
<cite ref="Shabbat 107a:3">Sabb. 107ᵃ</cite> <he>להוציא ממנה ל׳</he> to let the pus escape.
Makhsh. VI, 7 הל׳ סרוחה ill-smelling moisture (purulent substance); a. fr.—Trnsf. ל׳ סרוחה (product of) ill-smelling secretion, i.e. man.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:9:1">Cant. R. to VII, 9</cite> <he>אי רשע ל׳ ס׳</he> Oh, thou wicked mortal! <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 20:10">Ex. R. s. 20</cite>; a. e.
